data.title: Bisleri seeks FSSAI review over conflicting test results for Bengal batch
data.description:
Bisleri International has sought a review by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) over conflicting laboratory findings concerning a batch of its packaged drinking water manufactured at its facility in Telipara, Jalpaiguri district, West Bengal.
 
The development comes after the regulator prohibited the sale of the specific batch, identified as PB201, on August 12, 2026, following the detection of coliform bacteria in samples tested by its primary and referral laboratories. The FSSAI has also sanctioned prosecution against the company in the matter, according to reports.
 
“Bisleri International Private Limited had already recalled Batch PB201 of its packaged drinking water at the direction of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), which prohibited the sale of the batch on 12 August,” the company said in a statement.
 
 
Bisleri said that while the primary and referral laboratories reported the presence of coliform bacteria in the regulatory sample, independent tests commissioned by the company yielded different results.
 
The company said it had separately commissioned testing of samples from the same batch at an FSSAI-recognised laboratory, which found that the sample met the applicable standards for coliform bacteria and other food safety parameters.
 
Samples tested at another independent, FSSAI-recognised laboratory also met the prescribed standards, it added.
 
“The difference between the regulatory and independent findings warrants a thorough review. Bisleri calls upon FSSAI to examine the sampling process, testing methodology, laboratory findings and any factors that may have contributed to the variation in results,” the statement said.
 
“We expect this matter to be assessed against the same standards applied across the industry,” the company added, reiterating that it would continue to cooperate with FSSAI to establish the facts.
 
Bisleri said it maintained stringent quality controls involving more than 90 tests across its 10-step manufacturing process and asserted that its products remained safe for consumption.
 
This is the second recent instance of regulatory action by FSSAI against Bisleri over the quality of its packaged drinking water.
 
On Sunday, the food regulator said it had sanctioned prosecution against the company following the detection of bromate levels above permissible limits in a sample collected from its Goa manufacturing facility. Subsequent testing by a referral laboratory also flagged the presence of polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), according to the regulator.
 
The Goa case relates to a batch manufactured in September 2025 at the company's facility, one of its 143 manufacturing plants.
 
Bisleri had said FSSAI collected six samples from the facility on September 30, 2025. Initial testing found that five samples met the applicable standards, while the sixth recorded bromate levels of 12 micrograms per litre against the prescribed limit of 10 micrograms per litre.
 
Following an appeal by the company on November 22, 2025, the sample was sent to a referral laboratory for retesting.
 
The referral laboratory found bromate levels within the prescribed limit but separately flagged the presence of PAHs, the company said.
 
On November 23, FSSAI clarified that bromate levels in the retested sample were below the permissible limit. Bisleri subsequently welcomed the clarification, while pointing out that one of six samples tested in a subsequent round had reported PAHs at 0.144 micrograms per litre. Another sample from the same batch cleared all parameters.
 
The company said it had sought a retest of the PAH findings and that subsequent samples tested by FSSAI across its manufacturing facilities had not reported adverse PAH findings.
 
The two cases involve separate batches and manufacturing facilities, with the latest dispute concerning coliform bacteria in the West Bengal batch and the earlier one involving bromate and PAH findings in the Goa batch.

data.title: Indian markets rebound in November after months of underperformance: HSBC
data.description:
Indian financial markets have staged a broad-based recovery in November, reversing months of underperformance against emerging-market peers as falling crude oil prices, a correction in global artificial intelligence-related investments and renewed foreign fund inflows improved investor sentiment, HSBC Global Investment Research said.

Equities, the rupee and government bonds have all rallied, signalling a shift in market sentiment from risk-off to risk-on.

However, sustaining the gains into 2027 will require stronger domestic growth expectations and an improvement in banking-system liquidity, which could remain constrained as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) tightens monetary policy amid elevated inflation, the global brokerage said.

"India has moved from risk-off to risk-on. After underperforming the EM Index for most of 2026, Indian markets rebounded in November, outperforming across equities, FX and rates. The recovery was supported by falling oil prices, global investors de-risking from AI names and stronger foreign inflows," it said.

 

India had underperformed emerging markets across equities, foreign exchange and interest rates for much of 2026 before staging a sharp turnaround in November.

The Sensex has gained around 13 per cent month-to-date, while the rupee strengthened to its highest level in eight months, trading below 92.50 against the US dollar.

The yield on the benchmark 10-year government security fell by around 20 basis points, indicating a rally in bond prices despite tightening liquidity conditions.

The recovery has been supported by lower international crude oil prices and global investors reducing exposure to artificial intelligence-related stocks, both of which have helped improve sentiment towards Indian assets and encouraged foreign capital flows.

HSBC said the simultaneous improvement across equities, currency and government bonds, along with a positive correlation between equity and debt returns, points to a broad-based improvement in risk appetite.

The return of foreign investors has been a key factor behind November's market rebound, particularly in equities, although debt markets have also seen improved inflows.

Domestic investors have supported Indian markets over the past few years, helping cushion the impact of foreign portfolio outflows.

"While domestic investors are needed to make sure the markets don't fall, sharp increases in returns are typically led by foreign investor participation," the brokerage said.

HSBC's analysis using the Diebold-Yilmaz framework, which measures the transmission of shocks between different asset classes, found that currencies are the largest net transmitter of market shocks in India.

The latest recovery followed a similar pattern, with the rupee beginning to strengthen around the middle of October, ahead of the broader improvement in other asset classes.

The brokerage's multi-asset analysis suggests that the November rebound was not driven by one isolated market development but reflected improving sentiment across financial markets, with currency movements playing an important signalling role.

HSBC, however, cautioned that external factors alone may not be sufficient to sustain India's market performance in the coming year.

Its proprietary multi-asset model identifies two global and two domestic variables that explain a substantial part of returns across Indian asset classes. The model currently indicates that Indian equities remain undervalued relative to their model-implied returns.

The rupee and government bonds, in contrast, appear broadly fairly valued.

This suggests that equities have greater scope to catch up if the current favourable conditions persist. However, once the valuation gap closes, further gains will depend on an improvement in the variables driving the model's expected returns.

HSBC identifies banking-sector liquidity and expectations of potential economic growth as the two key domestic factors that need to improve.

Liquidity could remain under pressure as the RBI tightens monetary policy in response to elevated inflation, potentially limiting the availability of funds in the banking system.

Consequently, stronger growth expectations will become increasingly important in sustaining investor returns.

The brokerage sees a possible improvement in India's export competitiveness and foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows as potential catalysts.

India's goods exports rose 25 per cent year-on-year in the previous quarter, supported by a more competitive currency, trade agreements and exporters expanding into new markets.

HSBC said the increase in exports, alongside early signs of stronger FDI inflows, could help improve expectations of India's longer-term growth potential.

If these trends strengthen, they could provide the domestic economic support needed to sustain higher returns across Indian asset classes in 2027.

However, risks remain, including the possibility of renewed escalation in geopolitical tensions pushing oil prices higher and a revival of volatility in global technology stocks. HSBC remains positive on the AI theme for 2027 despite the recent correction.

Against this backdrop, HSBC's equity strategists remain overweight on Indian equities, citing resilient corporate earnings and more reasonable valuations following the period of underperformance.

The brokerage believes the improvement in valuations, combined with the prospect of sustained earnings growth, provides support for the market despite uncertainties surrounding global conditions and domestic liquidity.

Its rates strategists, meanwhile, have introduced a pay-five-year Non-DeliverableOvernight Index Swap (NDOIS) trade, reflecting expectations of tighter monetary policy amid the RBI's focus on inflation.

In foreign exchange, HSBC's strategists have lowered their USD-INR forecasts for the end of 2026 and 2027, signalling a more favourable outlook for the Indian currency.

The brokerage also prefers the rupee among Asian currencies in the deficit-currency category, reflecting its relative attractiveness in regional foreign-exchange carry trades.

data.title: Kharge hosts INDIA bloc meeting to discuss strategy on delimitation Bill
data.description:
INDIA bloc floor leaders met at Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge's residence here on Saturday and deliberated on a joint strategy in view of the government's imminent move to reintroduce a constitutional amendment bill in Parliament, involving delimitation.

Besides Congress president Kharge, former party chief Rahul Gandhi, TMC's Abhishek Banerjee, Independent Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal, RJD's Abhay Kumar Singh and Manoj Jha, CPI's P Sandosh Kumar, IUML's ET Mohammed Basheer, RSP's NK Premchandran, among others, participated in the meeting.

Congress general secretaries Jairam Ramesh, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and K C Venugopal, among others, also attended the meeting.

 

While non-INDIA bloc parties such as the DMK, AAP and BJD were also invited for the meeting, they chose to stay away.

"Look, we need to examine this from the perspective of what is going to happen at the national level and what lies ahead. At the national level, if this Bill is passed, the number of Lok Sabha seats could increase to around 850. The first question is whether a House of 850 members can function properly," Sibal told reporters ahead of the meeting.

"But the most serious issue is that their objective is not merely women's reservation. We are ready for women's reservation. They can implement it immediately within the existing 543 seats. So that is not their real objective. Their real objective is to remain in power for the next 30-40 years. And for that, what matters most to them is the Delimitation Bill," he said.

"They will make appointments to the delimitation body in the same way they appointed Gyanesh Kumar to the Election Commission. In other words, another Gyanesh Kumar will be placed in this position. They will decide the boundaries of constituencies in states such as Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Maharashtra according to their own preferences," he said.

This kind of manipulation is called gerrymandering and by carrying out such gerrymandering, they want to remain in power for the next 40 years, Sibal alleged.

"And after that, once they secure a two-thirds majority in Parliament, particularly if the strength of the House increases to 850 and they manage to get two-thirds of those seats, they will certainly change the Constitution," he said.

A special sitting of Parliament has been convened from November 30. The Lok Sabha has been reconvened on November 30 and the Rajya Sabha on December 2.

The sittings will conclude on December 3, subject to exigencies of government business.

The Centre is set to introduce a fresh constitutional amendment Bill in the Lok Sabha on Monday to roll out one-third reservation for women by increasing each state and Union territory's seat allocation in the House and the strength of their legislative assemblies by 50 per cent, and freeze the revised allocations and boundaries until 2051.

The Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, slated for introduction in the Lok Sabha on Monday, seeks to raise the House's maximum strength to 850, with up to 815 members from states and 35 from Union territories. It also proposes to raise the ceiling on the size of a state Assembly from 500 to 650.

The objective of the present Bill is to give immediate effect to one-third reservation for women, including women belonging to the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes, in the House of the People and the Legislative Assemblies of the States and the Union territories, through a delimitation exercise, the Bill's Statement of Objects and Reasons says.

It says the exercise shall provide for an increase of 50 per cent, in the number of seats in the House of the People and the Legislative Assemblies of the States and Union territories, over and above the number of seats existing immediately before such delimitation.

On April 17, the earlier constitutional amendment Bill fell 54 votes short of the required two-thirds majority in Lok Sabha, with 298 MPs voting in favour and 230 against. The government did not proceed with the accompanying bills.

The opposition has undergone a churn since then.

Twenty Trinamool Congress MPs broke away in June and announced their merger with the NDA-supporting Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI).

Disqualification proceedings against them are pending before Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla.

The NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar), which has eight MPs and opposed the April Bill, said on Friday that it would back the fresh proposal if it provided for a uniform 50 per cent increase.

The DMK, with 22 MPs, has also backed the bill.

The BJP is confident of securing the required two-thirds majority, banking on the Trinamool rebels and support from some other parties that opposed the Bill in April.

The Lok Sabha has 540 sitting members and three vacancies. If Trinamool MP Kalyan Banerjee's suspension remains in force, 539 members, including the Speaker, can attend the proceedings.

The Bill would need 359 votes if all 538 members other than the Speaker vote. Absent members would lower the two-thirds threshold.

data.title: Maritime security vital for global trade, economy, says President Murmu
data.description:
President Droupadi Murmu on Saturday said the maritime domain had become increasingly important in today's interconnected world, with a large part of global trade moving through the seas, and stressed that India was steadily strengthening its indigenous defence capabilities.

Addressing the passing-out parade of the Indian Naval Academy (INA) at Ezhimala here, she said the security of maritime routes was closely linked to the economic well-being of nations and the everyday lives of their people.

"The maritime domain has become increasingly important in today's interconnected world. A large part of global trade moves through the seas. The security of maritime routes is therefore closely linked to the economic well-being of nations and the everyday lives of their people," she said.

 

President said that any disruption in the movement of ships can affect the supply of essential goods, increase costs, and ultimately place an additional burden on ordinary citizens.

"You should remember that your service at sea is connected to the lives of the people of India. It contributes directly to their security, prosperity, and well-being," she said.

The President said India was also steadily strengthening its indigenous defence capabilities, with a growing number of ships and submarines being designed and built in Indian shipyards.

"This reflects our commitment to self-reliance and our confidence in the capabilities of our engineers, scientists, skilled workers, and industry. As an officer of the Indian Navy, you will be part of this journey towards a stronger and more self-reliant India," she said.

Noting that the world was changing at an unprecedented pace, Murmu said new technologies were transforming the nature of warfare and maritime security.

"We cannot predict all the challenges that the future will bring, but I am confident that your training, adaptability, and commitment will prepare you to face them. You should always continue to learn and should keep upgrading your knowledge and skills," she said.

The President said the ultimate purpose of all national efforts was to build a strong, prosperous and developed India.

The vision of Viksit Bharat was not limited to economic growth or improvement in development indicators. It was about creating a nation where every citizen felt secure, had access to opportunities and could lead a life of dignity and self-respect, she said.

It was also about ensuring that the benefits of development reached every section of society and every corner of the country, she said Referring to her participation in the International Fleet Review in Visakhapatnam in February this year, Murmu said it was an impressive demonstration of the Indian Navy's growing strength and capabilities.

India was making rapid progress in strengthening its armed forces and enhancing its maritime capabilities, she said.

Murmu expressed happiness over the presence of several young women among the graduating trainees and said their participation was a matter of pride for the entire nation.

"My dear daughters, your presence here is a matter of pride for the entire nation. You have demonstrated that determination, courage, and competence know no boundary. Your achievements will inspire many more young women to dream big and take up challenges and responsibilities in the service of the nation," she said.

Congratulating the graduating cadets, the President said they had successfully completed training that tested their physical endurance, mental strength and determination.

Their smart turnout, excellent military bearing and precision in performing the drill reflected the highest standards of training, discipline and dedication, she said.

Murmu also acknowledged the contribution of the parents and families of the graduating officers, saying that behind every young officer stood a family that had made sacrifices, offered encouragement and provided strength through difficult times.

She extended special congratulations to the trainees from friendly foreign countries and said it was heartening to see them marching shoulder to shoulder with their Indian counterparts.

"The friendships developed at the academy would go beyond the years spent there, and the trainees would carry forward the spirit of mutual trust, cooperation and friendship that bound their countries together, she said.

The President said the integrity, professional competence, courage and compassion of the officers would define the character of the Indian Navy.

"You should always remember that leadership is not merely about giving commands. It is about undertaking responsibility, setting an example, and standing by those who serve with you," she said.

A total of 427 officer trainees passed out as commissioned officers at the Indian Naval Academy.

Murmu first reviewed the platoons before receiving the salute from the marching contingent.

She also presented awards to the best-performing cadets at the academy, Keralam Governor Om Prakash Mathur, Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Southern Naval Command, Vice Admiral Sameer Saxena, and Commandant of the Indian Naval Academy, Vice Admiral Alok Ananda, were also present.

data.title: Delhi AQI remains 'poor' at 252; six stations record 'very poor' air
data.description:
Delhi's air quality continued to remain bad on Saturday, with the national capital's overall Air Quality Index (AQI) rising to 252 in the 'poor' category, according to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).
 
The reading, recorded at 9 am on November 28, was higher than the AQI of 226 on Friday. The city's AQI had stood at 224 on November 26 and 220 on November 25, indicating a gradual deterioration in air quality over the past three days.
 
Several monitoring stations across the national capital recorded AQI levels in the 'very poor' category, with CRRI Mathura Road reporting the highest reading of 333.
 
 
Chandni Chowk recorded an AQI of 325, followed by Delhi Technological University (DTU) at 317 and Wazirpur at 314. Pusa recorded an AQI of 310, while the reading at Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport stood at 309.
 
In contrast, Lodhi Road recorded the lowest AQI among the listed monitoring stations at 148, placing it in the 'moderate' category.
 
Under the CPCB's classification, an AQI between 0 and 50 is considered 'good', 51 and 100 'satisfactory', 101 and 200 'moderate', 201 and 300 'poor', 301 and 400 'very poor', and 401 and 500 'severe'.
 
Delhi weather today
 
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast mainly clear skies in Delhi on Saturday, with mist or shallow fog likely at a few places during the morning. The maximum temperature is expected to remain between 24 degrees Celsius and 26 degrees Celsius, while the minimum is likely to range from 8 degrees Celsius to 10 degrees Celsius.

data.title: Shinde orders crackdown on illegal hoardings in Thane, seeks new ad policy
data.description:
Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde has directed civic officials in Thane to crack down on unauthorised hoardings that are defacing the city and to frame a new advertising policy, officials said on Saturday.

Shinde, who is also the Guardian Minister of the district, has directed Thane Municipal Corporation (TMC) Commissioner Saurabh Rao to launch a special drive and impose heavy penalties and criminal cases against violators, an official release by his office said.

Alongside the enforcement drive, Shinde also suggested that the civic body formulate its own comprehensive new hoarding policy.

Under the proposed policy, he directed the administration to identify suitable locations across the city for installing digital hoardings and allow authorised advertisements against prescribed fees.

 

He noted that regulating outdoor advertising through digital hoardings would not only curb visual clutter but also boost the Thane Municipal Corporation's revenue.

data.title: DMK backs 50% Lok Sabha seat increase, seeks to protect Tamil Nadu's share
data.description:
Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) MP A Raja on Saturday said the party has decided to support the proposed 50 per cent increase in parliamentary seats across states, while reiterating that Tamil Nadu's existing share of representation in the Lok Sabha must remain protected amid the Centre's proposed delimitation exercise.

Speaking to ANI after the DMK meeting, Raja said the party's consistent demand had been that Tamil Nadu's 7.18 per cent share in the Lok Sabha should not be altered, adding that the proposed arrangement appeared to preserve the state's representation.

"Our consistent demand is that the share of 7.18% (seat share in Lok Sabha) should not be altered. Now it is being maintained. Of course, procedural issues are there; we will address them. If necessary, we will give an amendment," he said.

 

Addressing a press conference in Chennai, the DMK leader said the party had maintained a consistent position on protecting Tamil Nadu's representation, irrespective of whether it was in power or in the Opposition and whether it was part of an alliance or not.

He said the party's position followed discussions involving political parties and Chief Ministers from different states at a Joint Action Committee meeting convened in Chennai by former Chief Minister and DMK president M. K. Stalin.

"During the last delimitation process, during the restructuring, Tamil Nadu's share was 7.18. In India, which consists of various states with various nationalities, various languages, and various cultures, that share was carried out the last time during Indira Gandhi's period in 1971 without causing harm to the culture and civilisation of each linguistic state," Raja said.

He maintained that retaining the same share was central to the idea of fair delimitation and said the DMK had not deviated from this demand.

"That the same share should continue is what 'fair delimitation' means, and all parties in that alliance, including the Congress party, [said], 'We wanted to have a fair delimitation.' Nowhere, apart from the term 'fair delimitation'--apart from fair constituency delimitation--did anyone propose any new formula that day," he said.

Raja also rejected allegations that the DMK had changed its position after moving away from the INDIA bloc, calling such claims politically improper.

"So far as DMK is concerned, we maintained full consistency when we were in power, and we were out of power. So notwithstanding the political entity, notwithstanding the political power, we maintained our consistency that the share of Tamil Nadu, 7.18, should not be affected," he said.

Explaining the party's assessment of the proposed arrangement, Raja said Tamil Nadu had lost two seats during the 1971 delimitation exercise, but the current proposal did not entail a similar reduction. He said the state's share had instead reached 7.21 per cent from 7.18 per cent.

He further said the party had examined the proposed legislation with legal experts and lawyers and that its leadership had authorised it to consult other parties and discuss possible amendments with the government.

"Beyond this number, we agree with the number 59. Beyond that, regarding the Delimitation Commission, other processes, and wherever else there are difficulties, wherever there is apprehension, wherever we have reservations, we asked if we can bring amendments in Parliament if needed," he said.

Raja added that the party would raise its concerns in Parliament and seek changes to specific clauses if required. He also said the proposed arrangement would retain the existing state-wise representation ratio for another 25 years.

The DMK's position is significant as the party has 22 MPs in the Lok Sabha and its support could influence the outcome of the proposed legislation. The party had earlier demanded that Tamil Nadu's 7.18 per cent share in the Lok Sabha remain unchanged and that the existing proportion of representation among states, based on the 1971 Census, be retained for another 25 years.

The Union Cabinet has cleared a legislative package to facilitate delimitation and the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies. The Centre is set to introduce the Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, during the special session of Parliament beginning November 30.

The proposed legislation provides for a 50 per cent increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats allocated to each state and Union Territory, as well as the total number of seats in State Assemblies. If passed, the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha would increase to 850, while that of State Assemblies would rise to 650.

The Centre's proposal links the implementation of women's reservation, provided for under the 106th Constitutional Amendment in 2023, with the fresh delimitation exercise, with the government aiming to complete the process before the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.

The Opposition has supported women's reservation but objected to linking its implementation with delimitation. It has also demanded the use of the latest Census data instead of the 2011 figures. The Centre has proposed using the 2011 Census for redrawing constituencies and determining SC/ST-reserved seats, while retaining the 1971 population basis for state-wise allocation of Lok Sabha seats until 2051.

data.title: Bihar's 'Bahubalis' thrive as parties prize winnability over the law
data.description:
A lot of us Indians have been transfixed by the wedding of Bihar strongman and expelled Janata Dal (United) MLA Anant Singh’s daughter. Estimates vary, but it seems between 300,000 and 500,000 people attended the wedding in Mokama. Anant Singh, mind you, is under trial for murder, out on bail, with 27 other serious cases to his name.  
The highlight of the wedding was a horse race with a Thar for the winner, plus much celebration, festivity and unlimited food. TV channels, especially some Hindi channels, have been dining out on this, counting the rasgullas and gulab jamuns on the guests’ plates. I saw one where the guest said he had six of each and complained that the others had collected a dozen or more. The highlight for me, however, was this scene: Anant Singh on a Land Cruiser, in an open black jacket, waving his gamcha (shoulder-wrap) with one hand and twirling his moustache with the other; thousands screaming “chhote Sarkar, chhote Sarkar” (literally, younger master). That’s because his brother Dilip Singh, who died in 2006, was the “bade Sarkar” (the elder master).
 
The “bade Sarkar” passed on the baton flawlessly to his younger brother, making him the leading Bahubali (strongman) of Mokama, among the poorest parts of Bihar. No surprise then that Mokama has been under the sway of not just one Bahubali, but two competing and feuding dynasties. Important fact: Both are from the same (upper) caste, Bhumihar. Both have been much in demand by political parties. In politics anywhere, “winnability” usually is like the Gangajal that washes a candidate of all sins. This is only more pronounced in the Hindi heartland. 
The bade-chhote Sarkar’s rival has been Surajbhan Singh, a former MP but long since banned from contesting after his conviction in a 1992 murder case. It took a fast-track court until 2008 to convict him. But never mind, his wife Veena Devi picked up the mantle. She, too, is a former MP, though lately she’s been losing elections. The rivalry continues. The population is divided in its loyalties between the two dynasties. But, as you’d expect, more would always be on the winning side — Anant Singh’s. 
Let’s keep the focus on the man of the moment, the bride’s father. Anant Singh has led a charmed life. He has faced multiple cases, but nothing takes away his sheen or grip on power. Being in or out of jail doesn’t matter. He was jailed in 2019, for example, under multiple charges including under the draconian UAPA (Unlawful Activities Prevention Act) after at least one AK-47, 22 cartridges and two bombs were recovered from his home. That should’ve finished his political career. Not in Bihar though. 
In the 2020 state elections, he contested from jail and won. And which chief minister doesn’t want any MLA from anywhere to shore up their numbers? In Hindi heartland politics, nobody is immune from it. Not even ever-so-holier-than-cow Nitish Kumar. His government dropped the UAPA charges in the final chargesheet and Anant Singh was out on bail. Just how tightly have you fastened your seatbelts as I recount this story?  
He wouldn’t be Anant Singh if you could keep him away from “adventure” and he always looks well-equipped for it. See the pictures from the wedding, him strutting about in track pants, a zipped-up jacket, with a cowboy hat on his head and flip-flops (hawai chappals) on his feet, surrounded by a dozen-plus henchmen carrying rifles. At the wedding, the only role for the police was in traffic management. 
His latest “adventure” came during the campaign for the Assembly elections in the fall of 2025. In a clash, Dular Chand Yadav of Prashant Kishor’s Jan Suraj Party was killed. Anant Singh was charged for the murder. He campaigned from jail and won. Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan (Lalan) Singh, also from his caste, campaigned for him while he was in jail. That was an IOU.
In the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, Anant Singh fielded his wife, Nilam Devi, against Lalan Singh on a Congress ticket. Of course, she lost. But, by 2024, Anant Singh was campaigning for Lalan Singh in the general elections. If you think this movement from one side to the other is bewildering, it’s because every party loves to have a good “winnable” Bahubali. Now you understand why Lalan Singh campaigned for a former rival who was now jailed. In March this year, the Patna High Court granted him bail. That’s what the Supreme Court has now cancelled. He is to surrender on December 1. But, he’s been telling his crowds not to worry, the Supreme Court will give him bail within three months. 
Let’s stay with Mokama and check out the history of the “chhote-bade Sarkars”. In 1990 and 1995, elder brother Dilip Singh won on Janata Dal tickets. He subsequently became a member of the Legislative Council. 
In 2005 and 2010, Anant Singh won from the older brother’s constituency. In 2015, he left the JD(U), contested as an Independent and still won. The tables turned in 2020, but only in terms of party loyalties. Anant Singh won again, this time from the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD). You don’t need more evidence that everybody needs a Bahubali. Remember, even the Congress had fielded his wife in 2019. 
While the UAPA charges were dropped, Anant Singh was still disqualified as an MLA in 2022 for possessing illegal weapons. This was after his Arms Act conviction by the MP/MLA court. Wife Nilam Devi contested the bye-election from his seat and won, retaining the seat for the RJD. Subsequently, the High Court acquitted Anant Singh under the Arms Act charges.  
Mokama is about 90 km from Patna, and carries a curse of geology. A large part of it is a depression, also described as The Tal (the lake). It’s prone to regular floods even in normal rains. 
Like most of Bihar, its economy is based on remittances. The people young and old that remain, have very little to do. The Bahubalis, therefore, become providers of petty contracts and casual labour in their “real estate” projects, sand-mining (mostly illegal), and generally in manning their wide protection rackets. 
I can take you on a grand gangland tour of the Hindi heartland, but let’s stay with Bihar this week. It gave India one of its most notorious mafiosi, Shahabuddin, the “lord and master” of Siwan. For years, he ran his empire, ordered hits and hostage-taking for ransom from jail, even while serving life-term for murder. But his wife, Hena, and son Osama, now an RJD MLA, have kept the legacy alive. They aren’t politically untouchable. The more striking case, currently in the headlines, is Anand Mohan. The “don of Sheohar” was finally nailed when convicted for the 1994 murder of G Krishnaiah, an IAS officer and then district magistrate of Gopalganj. 
In 2023, Nitish Kumar amended Bihar’s prison remission rules in a manner you could only describe as designed bespoke for Anand Mohan. He lifted the restriction on remission for those convicted of killing public servants on duty. Anand Mohan is now out. It’s only this week that the Supreme Court quashed the Bihar Government’s customised remission policy. 
He will return to jail, like Anant Singh. But, even when he’s been away his wife, Lovely, and son Chetan have been contesting and often winning from the pocket borough. Both have been courted across parties. We could move to Pappu Yadav and his wife Ranjeet Ranjan.  But we will be moving into the territory of what young people call TMI, or too much detail. 
I can take you through the star cast of Bahubalis of neighbouring Uttar Pradesh, from Atiq Ahmed to the Ansaris and Hari Shankar Tiwari. But here’s the larger point: There may be a million problems that bedevil the Hindi Heartland, yet the love of the gangster is among the top three, along with caste and communalism. 
 
By special arrangement with ThePrint

data.title: Sharad Pawar's delimitation stand draws rebuke from Maharashtra Congress
data.description:
The Maharashtra Pradesh Congress Committee rebuked ally Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar) over the announcement that it will back the BJP-led central government on the proposed delimitation legislation.

In a post on X, the Maharashtra Congress reminded NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar and working president Supriya Sule that the Congress had sacrificed its own claim to a Rajya Sabha seat earlier this year to ensure the 85-year-old veteran leader was re-elected to the Upper House.

"The Congress party had stood firmly behind Sharad Pawar right to the end to send him back to the Rajya Sabha at the age of 85. Elections were due to be held in March 2026 for Maharashtra's 7 Rajya Sabha seats. The Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar) had just 10 MLAs. A candidate needed 36 votes to get elected. Congress had 16 MLAs, while Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray) had 20," he said.

 

The Maharashtra Congress further claimed that NCP-SP MP Supriya Sule had personally approached top Congress leaders seeking their backing for her father's nomination.

The Congress party decided to sacrifice its claim over the seat. However, now the same Sharad Pawar is backing the Delimitation Bill proposed by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

"Supriya Sule sought Congress leaders' support for Sharad Pawar's candidacy. Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge agreed without any hesitation. Congress set aside its claim to its own seat and supported Sharad Pawar's candidacy. Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray) then also backed him, and the Maha Vikas Aghadi unanimously confirmed his candidacy. And now what? Against the backdrop of the delimitation law, the same Sharad Pawar, Supriya Sule and their Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar) are going to support the BJP government," he said.

Earlier on Friday, NCP-SP leader Jitendra Awhad stated that the party will support the upcoming delimitation exercise, describing it as a constitutional obligation following discussions with party supremo Sharad Pawar.

Clarifying the nature of the deliberations, Awhad told reporters, "The discussion wasn't about our party's official stance. The general point being made was that the delimitation process is a constitutional requirement... A decision has been made to support the delimitation process, and we will indeed support it. We will support the delimitation."

The Delimitation Bill is proposed to increase the number of seats in the House to 850, with 815 seats proposed for the States and the remaining 35 for the Union Territories. The Lok Sabha has 543 seats at present.

This delimitation row has triggered political debate, after Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said the government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the Lower House on November 30 and the Upper House on December 2, respectively, to transact essential government business.

data.title: Tata Sons files caveats in Bombay HC, SC ahead of November 30 board meet
data.description:
Even after the Bombay High Court had wrapped up the Tata Trusts versus Tata Sons hearing for the day on Friday, allowing the Tata Sons board meeting to go on as scheduled on November 30, lawyers for the holding company of the conglomerate were working on a caveat. 
ALSO READ: Tata Sons listing, restructuring, EGM on November 30 board meet plan
 
Tata Sons is learnt to have filed a late evening caveat in the division bench of the Bombay High Court and the Supreme Court on November 27. The caveat is a precautionary step to ensure that the company is heard before any verdict is passed on an appeal challenging the Bombay High Court’s order. 
ALSO READ: Tata Sons should choose its future rather than face a forced listing
 
 
In a single-bench order on Friday, Justice Abhay Ahuja of the Bombay High Court refused to grant any interim relief to Tata Trusts, which holds 66 per cent in Tata Sons, while setting January 21, 2027, as the next date of hearing. This means that despite the Tata Sons board meeting proceeding on November 30 without any legal restraint, any board resolution will be subject to the final court order. 
ALSO READ: Inside the Tata Sons power struggle: The rules, the rift and the road ahead
 
Two entities of the Tata Trusts — Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and RD Tata Trust — had moved court on Thursday against Tata Sons and its directors, challenging the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as Tata Sons chairman for a third term. The Tata Trusts suit also sought a restraint on the November 30 board meeting agenda that includes a proposed listing of Tata Sons. Citing Section 121 of the Articles of Association (AoA) of Tata Sons, the petition asked the court to prevent a casting vote by Chandrasekaran or any other director in case of a tie, as had transpired during the contentious September 17 board meeting. 
Noel Tata, Tata Trusts chairman and nominee director on Tata Sons board, had voted against Chandrasekaran’s third term while Venu Srinivasan, the other nominee director, had voted in favour of the proposal on September 17, resulting in a tie, forcing a casting vote from acting chairman Harish Manwani. All board members, other than Noel Tata, backed the proposal. The development put a question mark on the definition of the affirmative vote in relation to Section 121, with varied legal interpretations.
 
Section 121 provides for additional voting requirement by nominee directors appointed by Tata Trusts as well as a casting vote by the chairman in case of a tie. Tata Trusts’ argument is that when the two nominee directors are split in their views, there is no affirmative majority and that a casting vote can’t be used in such a scenario. Tata Sons has maintained that the chairman can exercise a casting vote when the Trusts nominee votes are split.
